findings.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — After acquiring the write lock there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache, so multiple goroutines that raced past the RLock check (cache still nil, or cfg.Env==Dev) each serially redo the full CDN/file read and manifest parse instead of reusing the value the first writer just computed

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — In setting.Dev every call bypasses the cache short-circuit and takes the exclusive write lock, serializing all concurrent Dev requests through GetWebAssets even though this matches the pre-diff intent of always recomputing in Dev

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:35 — Data-race fix (new sync.RWMutex around entryPointAssetsCache) ships with no test file at all in pkg/api/webassets, so there is no regression coverage proving the race is fixed or would be caught if reintroduced
pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:38 — No test exercises concurrent goroutines calling GetWebAssets under `go test -race`, which is the standard way to validate a fix for a documented data race

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:45 — In setting.Dev every call bypasses the cache short-circuit and takes the exclusive write lock, serializing all concurrent Dev requests through GetWebAssets even though this matches the pre-diff intent of always recomputing in Dev

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and unconditionally takes the exclusive Lock() on the cache-miss path (after the dev short-circuit check). In setting.Dev, the function always bypasses the cache return and will always acquire the write lock, meaning concurrent Dev requests will be serialized through GetWebAssets. Pre-diff there was no locking, so Dev calls could run concurrently; this is a performance/concurrency concern introduced by the change rather than a correctness bug shown in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows adding an RWMutex around the global cache in pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go; it does not show the presence or absence of any *_test.go files in pkg/api/webassets, so the claim that there is “no test file at all” cannot be verified from this diff alone. The remainder of the finding is a generic request for regression coverage rather than a diff-grounded, specific issue.
